[1/6] Make the core values machine-checkable: a diagnostic code registry, an executable verifier, an agent capabilities manifest, a machine-code listing and a stdlib-only proof

impact_assessment.why: The stated core values (fast, no dependency, machine-level, verifiable, tested with error codes, agent-compatible) are currently claims in prose; only some are enforced by a gate.
impact_assessment.benefits: Each value becomes a command or a test an agent can run: verify proves an artifact's structure without executing it, capabilities publishes the surface as JSON, a listing shows the emitted instructions, and a test proves the compiler imports nothing outside the standard library.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new CLI subcommands and a codes registry become permanent; dependency: stdlib only must hold, so no third-party imports anywhere; concurrency: none; state: verification is read-only and never rewrites an artifact.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the registry generated from what the source emits and assert both directions against README, make verification pure over bytes, add no dependency, and run every gate.

checkpoints.description: Task 'cairn-verifiable-core' completed successfully.
[1/4] Bind the six core values (No Dependency, AI Compatible, Easily Understandable, Almost Machine Language Like, Verifiable, Error Codes) to executable evidence and a failing guard each

impact_assessment.why: The six core values are stated in prose and repeated by hand; a value with no check can silently stop being true, and an agent has no way to tell which command proves which value.
impact_assessment.benefits: One record per value with the command that demonstrates it and the test that fails when it breaks; the manifest publishes them, the README renders them, and a test asserts every guard resolves and every evidence names a real subcommand.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the value names, keys and order become permanent identifiers; dependency: stdlib only must keep holding; concurrency: none; state: read-only, values.py holds no state.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Freeze the six values and their order in an ADR, point each guard at an existing test instead of duplicating it, assert guard resolution with ast, and re-run every gate.

checkpoints.description: Task 'cairn-core-values' completed successfully.
[1/4] Plan: keep up to six parameters and locals in callee-saved registers, with a stack fallback and one epilogue

impact_assessment.why: Every local read and write is an rbp-relative load or store, and the hot benchmark loops spend most of their instructions moving values between rax and their frame slot; that slot traffic is the largest gap between Cairn and the C twin.
impact_assessment.benefits: The first six slots, parameters included, live in callee-saved registers for the whole function; only the registers a function actually uses are saved and restored, and functions with more than six slots keep the existing stack path.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: emitted code changes but the language surface does not; dependency: none, standard library only; concurrency: none; state: builds stay deterministic and no persisted format changes, but the ABI save and restore must be exact or a caller value is corrupted
impact_assessment.mitigation: A recording-assembler test proves a promoted slot never touches its frame slot, behaviour tests cover calls, recursion, more than six slots and a branch that never ran, and the differential optimised/unoptimised test and the benchmark harness run before and after

[1/3] Audit wave covering all 6 commits: enforce ASCII-only lexer to match documented contract

impact_assessment.why: Lexer accepts Unicode identifiers and digits via isalpha/isalnum/isdigit, contradicting ASCII-only contract and capabilities limits
impact_assessment.benefits: Restores documented ASCII-only surface, keeps E1001 as single unexpected-character path, prevents non-ASCII names slipping into slots and listings
impact_assessment.risks: contract: lexer tightens to reject previously accepted names, no new code; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: no persisted format change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first lexer test for non-ASCII, restrict digit/identifier scans to ASCII, re-run full unittest plus aikit check, keep E1001 code unchanged
